mm_per_unit_gap: apps/web/src/main.js's actual /generate POST body (runGenerate, ~line 3091) does NOT include mm_per_unit — only fp, boundary, entrance_point, typed_edges, requirements, swap. This script passes mm_per_unit=18000 (constants.js METRES_PER_UNIT*1000, == schema.SCALE) because that is the value the frontend's own scale convention implies, and generate()'s step-3 min_edge enforcement is OFF when mm_per_unit is absent (generate.py _min_edge() returns 0.0). The live app therefore never enforces min_edge during the solve; topo_sensors.check_min_room_size still judges with the correct scale only because its fallback (schema.SCALE) happens to equal the frontend's real scale.
label_canonicalization_bug: ROOT CAUSE, confirmed empirically (see per-room generate_report_min_edge_mm/generate_report_min_area_mm2, all 0.0 below): generate.py imports _label from rectangular_arrange (packages/floorplan_core/rectangular_arrange.py line 128: `room.get('label', room.get('type','unknown'))`, a raw passthrough, no normalisation). Source RPlan plan JSON carries BOTH type=<int 0-9> and label=<PascalCase string, e.g. 'Kitchen', 'DiningRoom', 'MasterBedroom'>. rectangular_arrange._label returns the raw label string, which never matches schema.MINIMUM_SIZES' lowercase/snake_case keys ('kitchen','dining','master_bedroom',...), so spec_from_plan()'s MINIMUM_SIZES.get(label,{}) is {} for every room, and demands[rid]['min_edge']/['min_area'] default to 0.0 universally. generate()'s step-3 solver (_min_edge(rid)) therefore enforces NO minimum room dimension for ANY room, independent of mm_per_unit, and report.rooms' min_edge/min_area fields (meant for UI/QA use) are always 0 too. topo_sensors.check_min_room_size uses topo_signature._label instead (packages/floorplan_core/topo_signature.py line 90), which DOES canonicalise (int type -> ROOM_TYPE_MAP, or string label lowercased + _LABEL_ALIAS), so it alone computes the true requirement and correctly flags violations the generator never tried to avoid. This is a data mismatch between two _label() implementations with the same name in different modules, not a geometry problem.

apply_best_expansion_finding: apply_best_expansion and check_plan_compliance live in packages/floorplan_core/fit_planner.py and are imported only by apps/api/server.py's /fit_harness route (around line 907), where check_plan_compliance gates a per-room compliance loop and apply_best_expansion applies the best interior-edge push move for a non-compliant room. /fit_harness belongs to the retired ARAP realiser lineage (ARCHITECTURE.md 'Retired / legacy'): it is absent from apps/web/vite.config.js's API_ROUTES proxy list and apps/web/src has no call to it, so no current route or frontend path uses these two functions — the live /generate path (Stage-0 node-driven solver) does not call them.
